panel_raw.steelman: The proposal is exemplary on the two things this lens most tests. First, gate clearance is scrupulously honest: it changes no `doctrine/` file, correctly declares the rate-limit gate (`rationale.md:323-347`) N/A, and pointedly declines the security/data-loss high-risk bypass rather than dressing "it's the differentiator / release blocker" as high-risk — the exact trap that killed a prior doctrine proposal. It routes the install-contract (`AGENTS.md:310-312`) and legal-instrument changes to review/Maintainer, not to the gate. Second, every doctrine and contract citation I opened is real and lands on the right lines (`runtime-contract.md:177-187`, `proposals.md:208`, `AGENTS.md:310-315`, all three LICENSE instruments, `CITATION.cff:18`, `install.py:1584-1592`). Both suppression directives (`claim-check-allow`, `cairn-internal-ref-allow`) are genuine, checker-recognized mechanisms used per convention. It invents no mechanism the doctrine already has, and correctly finds PROVENANCE doesn't cover license.

critiques.concern: P6's premise misreads the license instruments. It repeatedly calls the split 'code=.py, prose=.md' (Context el.6, P6) and says .yml/.txt config 'sit outside both declared license families.' But the instruments are concept-based, not extension-based: LICENSE-CC-BY.md:15-16 scopes MIT to 'source code (.py OR OTHER CODE)' and LICENSE-MIT.md:3-8 to 'all source code... wherever it lives'; the CC-BY families are 'prose, templates, and explanatory visuals' (LICENSE-CC-BY.md:5-13). A functional vendor_targets.yml is plausibly already MIT as 'other code' and is none of the prose/template/visual kinds. So P6 is either a mere clarification (and 'outside both families' is false) or a substantive coverage change (and cannot also be 'descriptive/procedural, routes nowhere'). This contradiction drives the routing question below.
critiques.grounding: LICENSE-CC-BY.md:15-16 ('.py or other code'); LICENSE-MIT.md:3-13; AGENTS.md:313-315 (both say 'code'/'source code', never '.py')
critiques.suggested_fix: Reframe P6 as a clarification that functional config/data files are 'other code' already covered by MIT Exception 1 (LICENSE-CC-BY.md:15-16), removing the 'outside both families' and 'code=.py, prose=.md' framing. This makes the routing claim ('none route to AGENTS.md/doctrine') true, since AGENTS.md:313-315's 'code is MIT wherever it lives' stays accurate.

critiques.concern: P6 edits only LICENSE-MIT.md, but the by-file split is stated in all three mutually-cross-referencing legal instruments (LICENSE-MIT.md:9-13, LICENSE-CC-BY.md:15-24 Exception 1, LICENSE-CC-BY-ND.md:18-27) plus summarized as a cross-cutting governing rule at AGENTS.md:313-315 whose invariant is 'Keep the three families from overlapping.' Adding a .yml/.txt disposition to one instrument leaves the other two's family statements incomplete relative to it, risking the drift the non-overlap invariant guards against. The 'Documentation / doctrine surface' section addresses only doctrine/ and AGENTS.md routing and is silent on three-instrument consistency.
critiques.grounding: LICENSE-MIT.md:9-13; LICENSE-CC-BY.md:15-24; LICENSE-CC-BY-ND.md:18-27; AGENTS.md:315 ('Keep the three families from overlapping')

critiques.concern: The AST-attestation re-anchor obligation is mis-attributed and its reasoning is inverted. P1 edits `_CORE_MAPPINGS` in `bootstrap/_scaffold/config.py` and P3 edits `bootstrap/_scaffold/install.py` (the lock dict) + `bootstrap/_scaffold/lockfile.py` (new readers). The committed baseline attests every top-level symbol of the whole `_scaffold` package — `Assign:_CORE_MAPPINGS` is a baseline key — and `ast_attest` is sensitive to global-binding value changes. AGENTS.md's operational-pitfalls bullet is bright-line: 'after any bootstrap/_scaffold/ change, re-anchor it per bootstrap/REANCHOR_RUNBOOK.md'. But the verification plan conditions the re-anchor ONLY on P2 SPDX headers ('If engine .py gain headers, re-anchor test_ast_attest.py'). Worse, P2's reasoning is backwards: the tool digests via `ast.dump(include_attributes=False)`, explicitly 'insensitive to line numbers, comments, and formatting', so an SPDX header (a leading comment) on `_scaffold/*.py` would NOT change the digest and would NOT trigger a re-anchor — while P1/P3's value/logic edits, which DO, are never named as re-anchor triggers.

critiques.concern: The `scripts/` count is wrong and the 'self-propagating into the adopter tree' mechanism does not apply to `scripts/`. The proposal says 'all 16 shipped .py under scripts/'; `find scripts -name '*.py'` returns 24. More fundamentally, the repo's `scripts/` is NOT an install source — every manifest SOURCE is rooted at `templates/` (0 sources begin `scripts/`); the 44 `.py` that ship come from `templates/…` and land at adopter `scripts/`, `tools/`, `.agents/`. Several `scripts/*.py` (quality_gate.py, check_cairn.py, measurements.py, token_budget.py …) have no template twin and never ship at all. Gate clearance is scrupulously honest: the proposal changes no `doctrine/` file, correctly declares the rate-limit gate (`rationale.md:323-347`) N/A, and pointedly declines the security/data-loss high-risk bypass rather than dressing "it's the differentiator / release blocker" as high-risk — the exact trap that killed a prior doctrine proposal. It routes the install-contract (`AGENTS.md:310-312`) and legal-instrument changes to review/Maintainer, and reserves the one genuine legal judgment (the CC-BY downstream-permission clause) and the notice home to the Maintainer. It is unusually well-grounded: the load-bearing legal fact reproduces exactly — `grep -rn "SPDX"/"Copyright (c)"` over `templates/`+`scripts/` returns zero header hits, so every shipped `.py` ships MIT-notice-stripped and no installed file carries CC-BY attribution — and the counts that matter reconcile (44 shipped `templates/` `.py`, 44 `.md` templates, 43 substituted+1 verbatim cached `.md` = 44, 94 manifest data rows), with machinery citations accurate (install.py lock dict 1584-93, base-cache 1558-62, `_LOCK_SCHEMA=1` at lockfile.py:42, `_cairn_version` reader 103-11). Both suppression directives (`claim-check-allow`, `cairn-internal-ref-allow`) are genuine, checker-recognized mechanisms; it invents no mechanism the doctrine already has, and correctly finds PROVENANCE doesn't cover license. Proportionality is exemplary: it discharges a real, verified pre-0.4 legal duty at near-zero ongoing adopter cost (one static repo-root NOTICE.md, invisible SPDX headers, one BOOTSTRAP paragraph), adds nothing to the always-loaded surface so Anchor 12's correctness cost (`rationale.md:144-169`) is not incurred, adds no new review apparatus (`dual-review.md:439-442`), honors the stdlib-only budget with a genuinely buildable P3, and follows the accepted review-record-integrity shape (fix live + record + guard).

numbered_critiques.concern: The AST-attestation re-anchor obligation is mis-attributed and its reasoning is inverted. P1 edits `_CORE_MAPPINGS` in `bootstrap/_scaffold/config.py` and P3 edits `install.py` (lock dict) + `lockfile.py` (new readers); the committed baseline attests every top-level symbol of the whole `_scaffold` package (`Assign:_CORE_MAPPINGS` is a baseline key) and `ast_attest` is sensitive to global-binding value changes, so AGENTS.md's bright-line pitfall ('after any bootstrap/_scaffold/ change, re-anchor per REANCHOR_RUNBOOK') applies to P1/P3. But the verification plan conditions the re-anchor ONLY on P2 SPDX headers. Worse, that reasoning is backwards: the tool digests via `ast.dump(include_attributes=False)`, explicitly insensitive to comments/formatting, so an SPDX header (a leading comment) would NOT change the digest and would NOT trigger a re-anchor — while P1/P3's value/logic edits, which DO, are never named as re-anchor triggers.

numbered_critiques.concern: P2's stated surface ('each shipped .py under templates/ and scripts/') conflates two different sets, the scripts/ count is wrong, and the 'self-propagating into the adopter tree' mechanism does not apply to scripts/. The self-propagation vehicle is the SOURCE tree templates/ (44 .py); every manifest SOURCE is rooted at templates/ (0 sources begin scripts/), and the 44 that ship land at adopter scripts/, tools/, .agents/. The repo's own scripts/ is a MIX — some are template duplicates, some are Cairn-self-only dev tooling that never installs (quality_gate.py, check_cairn.py, measurements.py, token_budget.py, verify_counts.py) — so headers on the repo's scripts/*.py do NOT travel into adopters; P2 conflates Cairn's own-repo MIT compliance with adopter self-propagation. The '16 shipped .py under scripts/' figure is top-level-only (omits the 8 shipped scripts/_onboarding/*.py); the recursive count is 24. Finally, byte-identical scripts<->templates twins (scripts/claim_check.py is IDENTICAL to templates/modules/default-on/claim_check.py; link_check.py and the _onboarding/* package similarly) mean a header applied to one side but not the other diverges them: no parity test was found to catch it (silent drift), and on the self-host side a header on an onboarding source must match its repo-root installed copy or the divergence/base-hash check reds.

numbered_critiques.concern: P6's assignment of .yml/.txt config to the MIT family is not the clean mechanical clarification the proposal frames it as, for two independently-grounded reasons. (a) The premise misreads the license instruments as extension-based ('code=.py, prose=.md'; config files 'sit outside both declared license families'), but the instruments are concept-based: LICENSE-CC-BY.md:15-16 scopes MIT to 'source code (.py OR OTHER CODE)' and LICENSE-MIT.md:3-8 to 'all source code... wherever it lives', while CC-BY covers 'prose, templates, and explanatory visuals' (LICENSE-CC-BY.md:5-13). A functional vendor_targets.yml is plausibly already MIT as 'other code' and is none of the prose/template/visual kinds — so P6 is either a mere clarification (and 'outside both families' is false) or a substantive coverage change (and cannot also be 'descriptive/procedural, routes nowhere'). (b) Either way P6 is a legal-instrument edit (LICENSE-MIT.md scope note) bundled into the recommended package, while the CC-BY downstream clause — also a legal-instrument edit — is reserved to the Maintainer on the stated principle that 'a legal-terms change is the Maintainer's call regardless of the doctrine gate'; that is inconsistent handling, and whether a .yml config counts as 'other code' is a legal-classification judgment that reallocates governing license for a whole file family, not a mechanical clarification.
numbered_critiques.grounding: LICENSE-CC-BY.md:15-16 ('.py or other code') and :5-19; LICENSE-MIT.md:3-13 and :14-19; AGENTS.md:313-315 (both say 'code'/'source code', never '.py'); the proposal's own Alternatives/rate-limit sections reserving the CC-BY clause as a legal-instrument change.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Reframe P6 as a clarification that functional config/data files are 'other code' already covered by MIT Exception 1 (LICENSE-CC-BY.md:15-16), removing the 'outside both families' and 'code=.py, prose=.md' framing (which makes the routing claim 'none route to AGENTS.md/doctrine' true since AGENTS.md:313-315's 'code is MIT wherever it lives' stays accurate); AND either reserve P6 to the Maintainer alongside the CC-BY clause, or state explicitly why an interpretive scope-note is safe to bundle when a permission-granting clause is not — getting the .yml/.txt='code' classification signed off, since it reallocates governing license for a whole file family.

numbered_critiques.concern: P6 edits only LICENSE-MIT.md, but the by-file split is stated in all three mutually-cross-referencing legal instruments (LICENSE-MIT.md:9-13, LICENSE-CC-BY.md:15-24 Exception 1, LICENSE-CC-BY-ND.md:18-27) plus summarized as a cross-cutting governing rule at AGENTS.md:313-315 whose invariant is 'Keep the three families from overlapping.' Adding a .yml/.txt disposition to one instrument leaves the other two's family statements incomplete relative to it, risking the drift the non-overlap invariant guards against. The 'Documentation / doctrine surface' section addresses only doctrine/ and AGENTS.md routing and is silent on three-instrument consistency.
numbered_critiques.grounding: LICENSE-MIT.md:9-13; LICENSE-CC-BY.md:15-24; LICENSE-CC-BY-ND.md:18-27; AGENTS.md:315 ('Keep the three families from overlapping').
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Have the plan decide one-canonical-home vs. mirror-in-all-three for the config-file disposition, and state it in the routing section. Given the instruments currently mirror each other, the safest is a single sentence placed consistently (or in one instrument with the other two pointing to it).

numbered_critiques.concern: P2 says add the header 'to the top of each shipped .py', but 34 of the shipped .py begin with a `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang, which must remain line 1 to stay executable. A header inserted at the true top breaks the shebang; it must follow it. The proposed mechanical grep-assertion test (invariant ii) must likewise accept a header on line 1 OR immediately after a shebang, or it will false-negative on every launcher/tool.

consolidated.coverage: Consolidated from three lenses that each swept the proposal's path:line and count claims against the tree this session, with substantial overlap and no contradictions in what was verified. Jointly verified: the SPDX/Copyright zero-hit grep over templates/+scripts/; the reconciling counts (44 templates/ .py, 44 .md templates, 43 substituted + 1 verbatim = 44 cached .md, 94 manifest data rows); install.py lock dict (1584-93), base-cache (1558-62), duplicate-destination guard (1348-54), divergence/base_hash (1547-48, 1559-69); lockfile.py `_LOCK_SCHEMA=1` (42), `_BASE_CACHE_REL` (40), `_cairn_version` (103-11), `_cairn_commit`->unknown (114-25); config.py `_CORE_MAPPINGS`(165)/`_SKILLS_MAPPINGS`(210-16, vendor_targets.yml@213)/`_ALWAYS_ON_MAPPINGS`(313); all three LICENSE instruments and their family definitions (MIT:3-33, CC-BY:5-24/45-48/54-62, CC-BY-ND:15-27); CITATION.cff repo URL(18) + license block(19-21, no CC-BY-ND); AGENTS.md install-contract(310-12)/license-split(313-15); doctrine/rationale rate-limit gate(323-347, bypass exhaustive to security+data-loss; gate correctly N/A, no doctrine/ change) + always-loaded cost(144-169); runtime-contract stdlib-only(177-187); proposals.md forward-reference-paths(208); PROVENANCE.md(59-63 safety-not-terms, 74-83 origin fields); DOCUMENTATION_PLAN routing(132-169)+paired-update(268-291); UPGRADE.md(28-35), BOOTSTRAP.md(288-304), case-studies/README(88-99), proposal template(69-70); both suppression directives against their real checkers (claim_check.py, check_cairn.py:401-405); broad-look Theme 4(288-310), A4(562-565), open-question-1(637-639). Empirically confirmed this session: the AST-attest suite is already red (2 failed / 24 passed on a clean tree) and a `_CORE_MAPPINGS` insert keeps it red; find scripts -name '*.py' = 24 (top-level 16); find templates -name '*.py' = 44; manifest has 0 sources beginning scripts/; diff scripts/claim_check.py <-> templates/modules/default-on/claim_check.py IDENTICAL; find dev/.cairn/base = 0 and grep base_cache dev/.cairn/cairn-lock.yml = 0; 34 templates/**/*.py carry a line-1 shebang. NEGATIVE SPACE (union of what no lens exercised): no full `pytest bootstrap/tests` clean baseline (the run timed out >2 min); no supervised REANCHOR flow run and no measured re-anchor diff for P1/P3; no actual scaffold install into a scratch target, so P1's lockfile files[]/manifest recording, P2's header round-trip, and NOTICE.md/lockfile-field/header presence in a real target tree are behaviorally unverified; install.py manifest/dup-guard/base-cache lines (1320-1562) not verified beyond the writer/base-cache blocks; and — flagged by every lens as outside the Internal lens — the load-bearing LEGAL-SUFFICIENCY judgment (whether one installed NOTICE.md plus self-propagating SPDX headers actually discharges MIT notice-retention and CC-BY attribution for files copied OUT of the tree) and the notice wording were not assessed.
consolidated.second_round_recommendation: Yes — all three lenses recommend an External (cross-type) read before the Decision, and the proposal itself sets Plan review = required(Internal) with External recommended, matching the standing workflow where a different agent type does External. The justification is strong and convergent: the change alters what every adopter tree redistributes (blast radius), it edits legal instruments (LICENSE-MIT.md in P6, plus the deferred CC-BY downstream clause), and — if P3 is kept — it touches the byte-level-stable install contract (AGENTS.md:310-12), so it warrants the tier that makes a change prove it should land, not just help it. Two facets specifically need a fresh, different-type read that sits outside the Internal doctrine lens: (a) the legal-sufficiency question of whether one NOTICE.md + self-propagating headers actually discharges the MIT/CC-BY obligations for files copied out of the tree (a legal-flavored judgment no test settles), and (b) the reserved CC-BY downstream-permission clause and the other Maintainer co-decisions (clause, notice home, the R5 P6-reservation call). External should also confirm the P6 reframe (R5), the three-instrument consistency decision (R6), and the .yml='code' classification. No blocking doctrine or gate defect stands in the way of the hand-off. Sequencing: land the Internal fixes first so External reasons over an accurate verification plan — correct the AST re-anchor scoping and the false green-baseline disclaimer (R1, R2), split P2's two populations and fix the 16->24 count (R3), and settle the split-P3 call (R4) so the External read evaluates the actual shipping unit rather than a bundle; the remaining framing/citation fixes (R7-R12) are author-resolvable pre-External.
